# Working from home: where do the hours go?

*Test fixture written for this repo. The numbers are illustrative.*

There are 24 hours in every day, and how we split them shapes our health and happiness. A typical full-time office worker sleeps about 7 hours, works about 8, and spends close to an hour a day travelling to and from work. Meals, chores and getting ready take another 3 hours or so. What is left is free time: on a typical workday, around 5 hours.

Working from home changes this split. The commute disappears, so in theory that hour goes back to you. Surveys find it rarely does all go to rest or hobbies. On average people who work from home spend about a third of their saved travel time working longer, and about a third on chores and family care. Only the rest becomes free time or sleep.

That still adds up. Even 20 extra minutes of free time a day is over an hour and a half across a working week.

The common belief is that working from home gives you back your whole commute. In practice the hours leak into longer workdays unless you protect them: a fixed finish time, a short walk to "end" the day, and a clear spot where work stays.

Not everyone gains. People with long commutes gain the most. People who live alone sometimes feel more isolated, and some find it harder to stop working at all.
